sources.title: A Walking Whale: Ambulocetus
sources.supports: Museum reconstruction and broad proportions: squat splayed legs, disproportionately large hind feet, approximate size and coastal-water context. Probable webbing is explicitly an inference.
sources.location: Main article and Extreme Mammals reconstruction photograph
sources.rights: Photograph credited © AMNH/D. Finnin. No redistribution permission asserted.
sources.use: Consulted for form; no photograph embedded in public model, textures or delivery.

sources.title: From Land to Water: the Origin of Whales, Dolphins, and Porpoises
sources.authors: J. G. M. Thewissen, Lisa Noelle Cooper, John C. George and Sunil Bajpai
sources.supports: Ambulocetid section and figures 15–16 distinguish fossil elements from a skeletal reconstruction. Four hind toes, five hand digits, larger feet than hands, long jaw, high lateral eyes and robust tail are stated; incomplete upper snout and few preserved tail vertebrae limit certainty.
sources.location: Ambulocetidae: the First Marine Cetaceans; figures 15 and 16; specimen H-GSP 18507
sources.rights: Open-access article; figure captions credit © J.G.M. Thewissen. No public image redistribution is claimed.
sources.use: Facts and anatomical interpretation only; reference images not embedded in public deliverables.

sources.title: Ambulocetus natans
sources.publisher: New York Institute of Technology, College of Osteopathic Medicine
sources.supports: Anatomy and locomotion summary: powerful legs and large feet, long robust tail likely without flukes, flexible neck and uncertainty in terrestrial locomotion. Gives approximate length rather than specimen measurements.
sources.location: Anatomy, Locomotion and Sensory Abilities sections
sources.rights: Institutional educational webpage; no image or text republication rights asserted.
sources.use: Consulted and paraphrased; no imagery incorporated.

sources.title: Additional holotype remains of Ambulocetus natans (Cetacea, Ambulocetidae), and their implications for locomotion in early whales
sources.authors: S. I. Madar, J. G. M. Thewissen and S. T. Hussain
sources.supports: Primary research abstract reports additional axial/pelvic material, approximately 80 percent skeletal completeness and a longer thoracolumbar region than some later archaeocetes. Supports a robust trunk rather than a minimal early speculative body.
sources.location: Journal of Vertebrate Paleontology 22(2):405–422; abstract only consulted
sources.rights: Publisher article, all rights reserved unless otherwise licensed. No full article or figures incorporated.
sources.use: Bibliographic/abstract fact check only. Full-text figures were not inspected.
